doc.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025

title: Learning songs and the illegal fake books
summary: Her teacher sold her an illegal fake book; she explains how the cards of melody, lyrics and chords were collected.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Well you’ve partly addressed this question but nowadays and for the last number of decades we’ve had much access to a great deal of material, first through printed fake books and now everything is online, you can get the chords on your phone and so forth. What did you do back then to learn these songs?

Well the piano teacher I had, after Miss Angstadt — who wouldn’t let me play anything but I did learn to read music and that’s good. But nevertheless when I was a senior in high school the piano teacher I had said, “I can get you a fake book. They’re illegal but I can get you one for $25 and this is what you should have.” So I still have my old first edition. And do you know where they came from?

Oh, well there used to be a service that would send to club date musicians — what we call club date musicians now — all the latest songs. And they were little cards like this and they had the melody and the lyrics and the chords. And somebody, I have no idea who, put them together three to a page. And that became the first fake book. And they were illegal because nobody was getting paid. None of the writers were getting paid for printing these. And so I have one and my first husband had one too, so I have two old fake books and you can find anything you know.
I wonder how you would have felt if you wrote a song and it showed up in these fake books where no one was getting any royalties etcetera.
Yeah. Well who’s getting what today anyhow when they can get a penny for something that got played in Portugal.
